name: mirage
text: Not by hand. The IRS wants a record that supports your totals, not a hand-written diary. A dated statement or export from the sportsbook or exchange showing wins and losses by bet is generally enough. Your Tracker already holds every bet with date, stake and result, and Novig's ledger has the same. So the job is to save a yearly export at year end, not to log anything yourself. Two things to know: (1) if you itemize, losses can only offset winnings, and the IRS has said it wants the session-level or net records, not necessarily every bet. Most people report total winnings and total losses from the annual statement. (2) the standard deduction is large, so at low income you may not itemize at all. Then losses give you no deduction and you simply report winnings. Note that the Tracker's 'bets' include your own taker bets, bids and engine orders, so exports should cover the whole Vigilant subaccount. This is general info, not tax advice. I can build the yearly winnings/losses export (CSV by venue) so you have it ready in January. Want that?
